attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, rebutting Frazier and Thierer, not quoting them.

semantics.note: Faithful. It keeps the 'will be absorbed' cost prediction, 'no serious argument' as his framing, the trillion-dollar scope and the hedged 'likely tied'. The firm 'will' makes this a scorable forecast. It has no deadline.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary: realized compliance costs that are immaterial to trillion-dollar firms, with no causal effect on the US-China race. 'Trivial' has no threshold and no deadline is given, so interpretation drives any verdict.

evidence.note: A Chamber of Commerce projection of economy-wide macro effects, extrapolated from Colorado. It does not measure realized compliance costs at trillion-dollar companies or any US-China capability effect.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. The packet has no company-specific realized compliance costs and no causal study of US-China capability effects. The only item is an opposing economy-wide projection, which the contract excludes. No early-resolution event is shown, so the evidence does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post.

semantics.note: The sentence sits inside a paragraph governed by 'if current trends continue', and it elaborates why the race ends without a victor. The normalised claim drops that proviso and lists no conditions. The contract restores the proviso, but the proposition overstates the commitment as unconditional.

contract.note: Reading this as US-China capability comparison under the trends proviso is fair, and the contract rightly refuses to add a deadline. Still, 'minimal' and 'short-lasting' have no thresholds, so interpretation decides. Condition_status 'not_applicable' conflicts with the contract treating the proviso as governing.

evidence.note: The Stanford AI Index (data to March 2026) reports US and Chinese models trading the top spot and a single-digit gap, 2.7% in March 2026. That supports 'minimal and short-lasting' for the period observed only.

IFP (19 Oct 2026) estimates a US lead of about 6.5 months on a different index. Whether that counts as minimal is unspecified, and it does not show a substantial, sustained lead with the trends continuing.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline, and its trends antecedent is not independently established. The AI Index shows a small, fluctuating gap through March 2026. IFP's 6.5-month lead estimate cuts against parity but sets no threshold. Finite observations cannot settle an open-ended forecast, and no conclusive contradiction meeting the early-resolution rule appears.
